summary: Reviewed all 20 unique paths and the subject of each image for every listed destination. The supplied destination associations total 24, not the stated 23 warning rows; I retained every listed destination ID. Unsplash’s direct pages were blocked by its BotStopper, so page-specific findings rely on indexed excerpts from official Unsplash pages; no credentials, login, or API-key attempts were made. Three photo-page excerpts explicitly exposed the matching CDN image path; other page matches are candidates, not confirmed mappings. No files were created or modified.

standard_license.quote: Unsplash grants you an irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide copyright license to download, copy, modify, distribute, perform, and use images from Unsplash for free, including for commercial purposes, without permission from or attributing the photographer or Unsplash.

attribution_guideline.quote: While the Unsplash License doesn’t require attribution because some uses may make it hard or impossible to attribute in a meaningful way...

shared_official_evidence.evidence_limit: The shared license and attribution policy establish Unsplash’s general rule, not that an unidentified image is covered by that license. CDN URLs were used only to inspect image content, never as licensing evidence.
